title: 環境化学
subtitle: Environmental Chemistry
educationalGoal:
Environmental chemistry deals with chemical reactions on the cyclical changes
and behavior of matter in the environment. You will learn the chemical reactions
related to the behavior of matter and energy in the atmosphere, lithosphere,
and hydrosphere to understand the ecosystem of the hydrosphere. The goal is
to gain an understanding of the limnological environment from published data
and to contribute to the conservation of the aquatic environment.
advice:
1.	Structure of the earth, global energy balance, and greenhouse effect.
2.	Cycles of matter, such as the carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorous cycle in the environment.
3.	Introduction to the aquatic environment and water cycle.
4.	Chemistry of water.
5.	Acidity of environmental water and acid rain issues.
6.	Oxidation and reduction in limnological environments.
7.	Effect of dissolution of substances on water quality.
books: Textbook: Limnological Chemistry, Kaoru Fujinaga (Ed.), Kyoritsu Shuppan
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of high school level chemistry and biology is required to understand the lectures.

activityGoals.body: Comprehend the meaning of technical terms.
Explain the carbon and nitrogen cycles.
Understand the relation between the water and energy cycles.
Describe the effect of water characteristics on the global environment.
Explain the effect of acidity on environmental water.
Explain the seasonal variation in the water quality of a lake.

achievementLevels.ideal:
Has an understanding of:
・ Technical terms in environmental chemistry
・ The carbon and nitrogen cycles in the environment
・ Effects of water acidity
・ Relation between rainwater pH and acid rain
・ Oxidation and reduction in terrestrial waters

Must also be able to understand newspaper articles about chemical species and to distinguish between scientific accuracy and bias.
achievementLevels.standard:
Using references, such as textbooks and dictionaries, can explain:
・ Technical terms in environmental chemistry
・ Cycles of matter in the environment, such as the carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycles
・ Effects of water acidity
・ Relation between rainwater pH and acid rain
・ Oxidation and reduction in terrestrial waters
・ Relation between dissolution equilibrium and terrestrial water quality
